title: Forking independence coincides with tensor independence in the r-space theories of the paper
author: John Baldwin, James Freitag, Scott Mutchnik
authors: John Baldwin, James Freitag, Scott Mutchnik
work: Simple Homogeneous Structures and Indiscernible Sequence Invariants
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies two independence relations in the r-space theories of the paper: forking independence over C and tensor independence, the latter being free amalgamation of the algebraic closures (statement lines 1089-1091). The proof disposes of one direction through invariant global types and reduces the other to the case where C is contained in an algebraically closed B, then finishes by the author's own claim about a C-indiscernible sequence of copies of B (proof lines 1111-1115 and the claim at 1124-1128). The step that carries the content is the proof of that claim, which splits according to the two ways tensor dependence can fail - either the algebraic closure is not larger than the union, or it is strictly larger - and in each case exhibits a finite set of neighbours witnessing the dependence of the next copy (proof lines 1133-1169). The author explicitly closes the main proof by pointing at the claim, so the claim and its proof are counted as the continuation of the same proof. H2.
